# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by sdk/python/tests/_reference_docs.py; a test keeps it equal. -->

Every `fabric` command and its options, as `fabric COMMAND --help` prints them.
Options on every command: `--config PATH`, `--project NAME`, `--json`, `--quiet`,
`--no-color`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check did not pass, 2 usage or configuration
error, 3 a prerequisite is missing; `fabric run` exits with the agent's code.

## fabric plan

Predict what Fabric would record for this project.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--kubernetes` | read the cluster of the current kube context (read-only) and predict what Fabric would record there |
| `--namespace NS` | the release's namespace (default fabric-system; found by itself when there is one release) |
| `--mcp-config PATH` | an MCP client configuration (a JSON object with mcpServers); repeatable |
| `-- CMD [ARGS...]` | the agent command (default: the project directory's language) |

## fabric init

Write fabric.yaml, generated secrets and the compiled environment.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--profile {local,production}` |  |
| `--production` | the production profile (same as --profile production): tokens, client certificates, an encrypted spool and a capture policy written into the project |
| `--shape {laptop,linux-host,container,kubernetes}` |  |
| `--tenant ID` |  |
| `--agent ID` |  |
| `--provider [DIALECT=]URL` | a model endpoint outside the built-in table, by its base URL |
| `--destination PRESET` | where records go: local-dir (local), trial, s3, s3-compatible or otlp (production) |
| `--bucket NAME` | s3, s3-compatible: the bucket |
| `--region NAME` | s3, s3-compatible: its region |
| `--sse-kms-key KEY` | s3: the KMS key id or ARN |
| `--endpoint URL` | s3-compatible: the store's https URL |
| `--ca-file PATH` | s3-compatible: the store's private CA certificate |
| `--credentials-file PATH` | s3-compatible: an AWS credentials file the Node reads |
| `--otlp-endpoint URL` | otlp, s3, s3-compatible: your OTLP/HTTP collector, where spans go |
| `--otlp-ca-file PATH` | the collector's private CA certificate |
| `--otlp-headers-file PATH` | a file with the collector's headers (Authorization=...) |
| `--queue-size SIZE` | the disk the Node's durable queue may use (20GiB, 500MB, or auto: half the free space) |
| `--image-digest sha256:HEX` | production: the agent image's digest, written into the capture policy |
| `--exec` | record the commands the agent runs |
| `--http-host HOST` | a non-model HTTP host to record |
| `--mcp` | record MCP transport messages |
| `--sensor {auto,ebpf,auditd,off}` |  |
| `--from-env` | import the `FABRIC_*` and `OTEL_*` settings of this shell |
| `--import-secrets` | with --from-env: copy the id key and CA into the secrets directory |
| `--rotate NAME` | rotate a generated secret: node-cert, ca, id-key, tokens or client-certs (production), or all (every one but the id key) |
| `--force` | rewrite fabric.yaml from the defaults and flags (keeps a backup, the project name and where its secrets are) |
| `--kubernetes` | create the missing Secrets in the current kube context |
| `--namespace NS` | the release namespace (default fabric-system) |
| `--agent-namespace NS[=SOURCE]` | a namespace whose agents send to the Node (repeatable); SOURCE is their source label (default the namespace name) |
| `--render DIR` | write the Secrets as manifests into DIR instead (GitOps) |
| `--release NAME` | the Helm release name (default fabric) |
| `--injector` | also the pod injector's serving certificate |
| `--content` | with --profile production: also the Node's content key |
| `--host-sensor` | with --profile production: also the Secrets of the chart's host sensor DaemonSet (the shared id key, its client certificate and one Secret per --host-node) |
| `--host-node NODE` | a node that runs the host sensor (repeatable), as `kubectl get nodes` names it |
| `--cluster-domain DOMAIN` | default cluster.local |
| `--in-cluster` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--node-service NODE_SERVICE` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--injector-service INJECTOR_SERVICE` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--secret-name ROLE=NAME` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--webhook NAME` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--from-env-file FILE` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--from-values FILE` | ==SUPPRESS== |

## fabric up

Start the local Fabric Node and destination, or install the Helm release.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--no-sensor` | do not start the host sensor |
| `--provider [DIALECT=]URL` | a model endpoint outside the built-in table, by its base URL (added to fabric.yaml as `fabric init --provider` adds it) |
| `--wait SECONDS` | how long to wait for the Node to answer (default 60; with --kubernetes, how long Helm waits for the release, default 300) |
| `--verify-images` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--kubernetes` | install the Fabric release into the cluster of the current kube context with Helm |
| `--namespace NS` | the release's namespace (default fabric-system) |
| `--release NAME` | the Helm release name (default fabric) |
| `--preset {local,production,production-host-sensor}` | the chart preset (default local: a trial Node; the production presets need your destination, given with --values or --set) |
| `--tenant ID` | the tenant id (default: fabric.yaml's, when there is one) |
| `--agent-namespace NS` | a namespace whose agents send to the Node (repeatable) |
| `--injector` | install the opt-in pod injector for the agent namespaces |
| `--values FILE` | a Helm values file of your own (repeatable; wins over the preset) |
| `--set KEY=VALUE` | a Helm value of your own (repeatable; never a secret) |
| `--chart REF` | the chart to install (default: this CLI release's chart) |
| `--host-node NODE` | with --render and the host sensor: a node that runs it (repeatable; default: read from the cluster) |
| `--render DIR` | write the Helm values and the Secret manifests into DIR for your own pipeline instead of installing |

## fabric down

Stop what `fabric up` started.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--purge` | also delete the project's volumes and .fabric/state (never the secrets directory or recorded data) |
| `--kubernetes` | remove the Fabric release from the cluster of the current kube context |
| `--namespace NS` | the release's namespace (default fabric-system) |
| `--release NAME` | the Helm release name (default fabric) |

## fabric run

Run an agent command with capture on.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--run NAME` | label this run (default: a fresh run-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxx) |
| `--exec` | replace fabric with the agent (the default on POSIX) |
| `--no-exec` | start the agent as a child, wait, and exit with its code |
| `--no-capture` | run the agent with its environment unchanged |
| `--print-env` | print the environment for an existing launcher instead |
| `--format {sh,dotenv,docker,systemd,k8s}` | --print-env format: sh, dotenv, docker, systemd or k8s |
| `-- CMD [ARGS...]` | the agent command |

## fabric verify

Check that a recorded run reached the destination intact.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `RUN` | the run label to read (default: the last `fabric run`) |
| `--canary-only` | check the path with the canary; do not read a run |
| `--spans PATH` | read the run from this span export (a destination Fabric cannot read back) |
| `--strict` | a warning fails too |
| `--wait SECONDS` | how long to wait for records to reach the destination (default 30; with --kubernetes and --spans, 180: for a run of the pods your rollout restarted) |
| `--production` | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--kubernetes` | check the Fabric release in the cluster of the current kube context (read-only), then read the run from --spans |
| `--namespace NS` | the release's namespace (default fabric-system; found by itself when there is one release) |

## fabric doctor

Check this machine and project for setup problems.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--kubernetes` | diagnose the Fabric release in the cluster of the current kube context (read-only) |
| `--namespace NS` | the release's namespace (default fabric-system; found by itself when there is one release) |

## fabric show

Show recorded runs.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `RUN` | the run label (default: the last `fabric run`) |
| `--list` | list recent runs with verdicts |
| `--actions` | the reader's action view |
| `--transcript` | the conversation only |
| `--content` | print content even when stdout is not a terminal |

## fabric version

Print the CLI, SDK and endpoint-table versions.

## fabric help

Show this help.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `topic` | a command |
